findings.title: verbs.md lists Init.migrate_seeds as a verb, but it is not one
locations: src/CLI/Init.jl:574-575: only `VERBS["migrate baselines"] = cmd_migrate_baselines` and `VERBS["new"] = cmd_new` are registered — no `migrate seeds` key exists
findings.description: verbs.md opens with "`gbg <noun> <verb>` is the whole command line; the table is closed, and every verb below is rendered from its own docstring so the page cannot drift from the code." `Init.migrate_seeds` is placed under "Consumer setup" alongside genuine verbs (`Init.init`, `Sync.sync`, `cmd_config`, `cmd_schema`), implying `gbg migrate seeds` is invocable. It is not: `migrate_seeds` is only ever called internally from `init(...; migrate = true)` (src/CLI/Init.jl:309-310); there is no `VERBS["migrate seeds"]` entry, so `gbg migrate seeds` fails with "unknown verb". The closed-table claim is therefore false for this entry.
findings.resolution_hint: Move `GBGCodingTools.Init.migrate_seeds` off verbs.md onto CLI.md's "Engines" section next to `Init.derive_config` (an internal helper `gbg init --migrate` calls), the way `derive_config` is already placed there rather than on the verbs page.

findings.title: Options, the record parse_options returns, has no home on any page
locations: src/CLI/Main.jl:12-24: `struct Options` carries a full docstring ("The fields are: positional, flags, values") that is never referenced by any `@docs` block
findings.description: `parse_options(args; valued = String[]) -> Options` is shown on verbs.md with no link to `Options`, and a whole-repo search of docs/src finds zero mentions of `GBGCodingTools.Options` anywhere. The type already carries a complete, correctly bulleted docstring (RULE.DOC.FIELDS-compliant) that simply is never rendered. A reader who wants to know what `.positional`, `.flags` and `.values` mean has no page to consult, contra RULE.DOC.API_GROUPING's "every derived public operation has a home on a public page."
findings.resolution_hint: Add `GBGCodingTools.Options` to verbs.md's "Entry point" `@docs` block, right after `parse_options`.

findings.title: gbg doctor's real CLI flags are undocumented on every page
locations: src/CLI/Doctor.jl:739-744: `cmd_doctor`'s docstring states `--deep`, `--json`, `--effective`, `--only <id-or-prefix>[,…]|QUICK`, and "exit 2 when the working directory is not a consumer"
findings.description: `cmd_doctor` — the function actually invoked by `gbg doctor [--deep] [--json] [--effective] [--only …]` and the only place its flags and its "not a consumer" exit-2 behavior are stated — appears in zero `@docs` blocks anywhere under docs/src (confirmed by grepping the whole tree; it only shows up in docs/prose_shape.csv, the baseline file). The docstrings shown instead (`Doctor.run`, `doctor`) use different Julia keyword names (`only`, `deep`, `json`, `effective`) and never spell out the `--` flag syntax. index.md calls `gbg doctor` one of "the two a person runs most," yet its literal command-line grammar has no page.
findings.resolution_hint: Add `GBGCodingTools.Doctor.cmd_doctor` to verbs.md's "Checks and scans" `@docs` block alongside `Doctor.run`.

findings.title: gbg scan docs's --rebaseline mode is undocumented on every page
locations: src/Scan.jl:549-554: `cmd_scan`'s docstring documents `gbg scan docs [--hard-only] [--only id,…] [--rebaseline prose-shape --reason "…"]`, which writes `docs/prose_shape.csv`
findings.description: `cmd_scan` is never referenced by any `@docs` block in docs/src (confirmed by a whole-tree grep; only docs/prose_shape.csv's baseline row mentions the name). `scan_docs`'s own docstring (src/Scan.jl:406-419), the one actually shown, says nothing about `--rebaseline` — a distinct, real operating mode (rewriting the RULE.DOC.SHAPE baseline) that is otherwise completely absent from the built documentation.
findings.resolution_hint: Add `GBGCodingTools.cmd_scan` to verbs.md's "Checks and scans" `@docs` block, or fold a `--rebaseline` sentence into `scan_docs`'s own docstring.

findings.title: install.md's shim description omits the fixture-routing exception
locations: docs/src/guide/install.md:35: "reads the pinned version, and executes `julia --project=<root>/docs` on the copy that environment resolved — so `gbg` in a consumer always runs that consumer's pinned version."
bin/gbg:19-22: `if [ "$v" = "dev" ] && ! grep -q '^name = "GBGCodingTools"' "$d/Project.toml" ...; then ... P=$r` (comment: "the fixture: enclosing tool repo")
findings.description: The shim has a third routing branch besides `--dev` and "the ordinary route": a consumer pinned at `dev` that is NOT itself the GBGCodingTools checkout (the fixture nested under the tool's own tree) resolves `--project=<enclosing tool repository root>`, not `<root>/docs>` as install.md's prose states unconditionally ("always runs that consumer's pinned version" via `<root>/docs`). The code's own comment calls this case out by name ("the ordinary route" vs. "the fixture"), so the omission is a real gap, not an edge case nobody anticipated.
findings.resolution_hint: Add a sentence after the `<root>/docs` claim noting the one exception: a `dev`-pinned consumer nested inside the tool's own checkout (the fixture) resolves against the enclosing tool root instead.

findings.title: rounds.md's gate description omits the audit's own GBG_ROUND export
locations: docs/src/guide/rounds.md:43-44: "the one named in `GBG_ROUND` …, which the CLI exports only while it runs a build or a test on that round's behalf."
src/CLI/Audit.jl:13-16: `audit_bank` runs `package.julia_test` AND every `executable_claims` command "with `GBG_ROUND` exported"
findings.description: `Gate.jl`'s own docstring (src/CLI/Gate.jl:9) is careful to say GBG_ROUND is exported "while it runs a build, a test or an executable claim," but rounds.md compresses this to "a build or a test," dropping the audit's executable-claims case entirely — the one place GBG_ROUND is exported for something other than `docs_build`/`julia_test`.
findings.resolution_hint: Add "or an audit's executable claim" to the "build or a test" phrase in rounds.md's gate paragraph.

findings.title: config.md's [surfaces] enumeration omits two schema keys
locations: docs/src/guide/config.md:11-13: "[surfaces] (the ONE copy of every surface list: rationale documents, pages, generated copies, source, extensions, Literate examples, the built site, the history and references anchors)"
schema/config.schema.json: `surfaces.properties` also carries `glossary` (a string path) and `data` (an optional list of data/script files whose comments are prose)
findings.description: config.md bills the `[surfaces]` list as "the ONE copy of every surface list" and enumerates it in detail (matching all 4 keys of `[docs]` exactly), but of the 11 actual `surfaces.*` schema keys (rationale, pages, generated, src, ext, literate, built_html, history_exempt, references_heading, glossary, data) only 9 are named — `glossary` and `data` are missing, so the claim to completeness is not met for this one section even though the adjacent `[docs]` enumeration is exhaustive.
findings.resolution_hint: Add "the glossary file, and any data/script surface" to the surfaces parenthetical.
